title: A builder sized up front

blocks.text: A builder's capacity is the room it has allocated; its length is how much text it holds. `new StringBuilder()` starts with room for 16 characters and grows as needed; `new StringBuilder(n)` starts with room for `n`, which saves regrowing when the final length is known. A negative capacity throws `NegativeArraySizeException`, a poor message for a caller's mistake.
Write `forLength(int expectedLength)` in `Capacity`. It returns an empty `StringBuilder` whose capacity is exactly `expectedLength`:

concepts: A builder's capacity is the space allocated, separate from its length; it can be set up front, and a negative capacity throws.
